items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-117518 has been identified in @fastify/reply-from versions up to and including 12.8.0. The flaw stems from the WHATWG URL parser normalizing backslash characters and percent-encoded forms to forward slashes, allowing path traversal checks to be bypassed using backslash dot-segments. Attackers can leverage this to send unauthenticated requests that escape intended upstream route prefixes, impacting confidentiality. The issue has been patched in version 12.8.1 by rejecting ambiguous whitespace, control characters, and single or double dot segments.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade @fastify/reply-from to 12.8.1 immediately to fix a high-severity path traversal vulnerability.

items.title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
items.one_liner: Evaluating LLM-driven verified code generation reveals that high verifier acceptance rates mask severe gaps in specification binding and semantic fidelity.
items.summary: Researchers argue that single-number verification metrics in LLM-driven verified code generation collapse three distinct failure surfaces: verifier acceptance (Surface A), syntactic specification binding (Surface B: proof obligation binding), and semantic specification fidelity (Surface C: informal requirement capture). Empirical demonstrations using Dafny-as-intermediate-representation pipelines on Python and Rust benchmarks reveal these surfaces separate significantly. Specifically, Claude Opus achieved 99.1 percent verifier acceptance on HumanEval while only 1.9 percent carried a certificate binding to a spec-defined predicate, and fully-verifiable Rust pipelines still experienced up to 14.82 percent failure on hidden tests.
items.bottom_line: High verifier acceptance numbers in LLM code generation do not guarantee that proofs properly bind to specifications or fulfill semantic requirements.

items.title: X.js: A Live Benchmark for Node.js Taint-Style Vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: X.js is a live benchmark of 1,159 validated exploits for Node.js taint vulnerabilities, showing a shift toward larger, complex packages.
items.summary: Researchers introduced X.js, a live benchmark designed to track and evaluate taint-style vulnerabilities across the Node.js and npm ecosystem, addressing a gap left by older datasets that stopped in 2022. Built from 1,738 advisories collected through mid-2026 primarily via the GitHub Advisory Database, X.js provides 1,159 validated exploits across 965 packages covering code injection, command injection, prototype pollution, and path traversal. To ensure long-term reproducibility, dependencies are hosted in a self-hosted registry, and automated infrastructure continuously validates new exploits. The study reveals that vulnerabilities are increasingly concentrated in larger packages, with the median package size jumping from roughly 250 lines of code in 2021-2022 to 6,100 lines of code in 2026.
items.bottom_line: X.js provides a robust, continuously updated benchmark for Node.js taint vulnerabilities, highlighting that modern vulnerable packages have grown significantly larger over time.

items.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
items.one_liner: HarnessFlow uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to automate and optimize LLM agent harnesses efficiently.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced HarnessFlow, an automated framework designed to optimize executable harnesses for Large Language Model agents using a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) policy. By navigating refinement attempts with archived code, execution feedback, and reusable mechanisms, HarnessFlow balances exploration and exploitation under a limited budget. On six benchmarks covering coding, web interaction, and agentic tasks, HarnessFlow-optimized harnesses achieved an average score of 69.48%, outperforming baseline models while maintaining lower per-task execution costs.
items.bottom_line: HarnessFlow offers an automated, MCTS-guided approach to optimize LLM agent harnesses with higher scores and lower costs.

items.title: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents
items.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation enables weight memory to rival text-based retrieval in LLM agents with lower token costs.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) to make weight memory competitive with text-based systems for long-term factual storage in LLM agents. By training a context-free student model from a teacher model conditioned on user memory alongside a verify-then-regenerate router, OPSD matches or outperforms strong text-memory baselines on the HaluMem benchmark while processing fewer tokens per query. This approach offers a low-cost memory alternative for persistent, multi-session agent deployments.
items.bottom_line: OPSD makes model weight memory a viable, low-cost long-term factual store for multi-session LLM agents.

items.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
items.one_liner: Four deaths in Ujjain highlight India's persistent crisis of fatal sewer and septic tank cleaning accidents.
items.summary: India continues to lose sanitation workers to hazardous sewer and septic tank cleaning conditions despite existing legislation, Supreme Court directives, and mechanised cleaning programs. Four workers recently died in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, while cleaning a hotel food-waste chamber, highlighting ongoing enforcement gaps and under-reporting by municipal bodies and private contractors who hire undocumented daily-wage workers. Although courts have mandated compensation up to ₹30 lakh and ordered an end to manual cleaning in major metropolitan areas, systemic failures in formalizing worker employment and safety oversight persist.
items.bottom_line: Systemic safety failures and illegal manual cleaning continue to cause preventable sanitation worker fatalities across India.
